beats.say: A password manager spots a fake site better than you: it checks the address letter by letter.
If the address differs even slightly, the manager offers no password. That is your warning sign.
Do not copy the password from the vault and paste it yourself. Check the address first.
Reject any approval request you did not expect: it means someone knows your password.

scenes.title: Test the autofill
scenes.intro: ParolSeyf runs in your browser. On every page, watch what it offers and check the address.

steps.say: ParolSeyf offers your login. Check the address.

actions.label: Fill with ParolSeyf
actions.feedback: Right. The address matches the saved login, which is why the manager offered it.

actions.label: Close tab
actions.feedback: Caution is fine, but this is the real office portal and the manager recognised it.

steps.say: A link in an email opened this page. ParolSeyf stays silent.

actions.label: Type the password by hand
actions.feedback: The manager stayed silent because this is a fake site. Change the password on the real portal now and report it.

actions.label: Find it in ParolSeyf and fill
actions.feedback: The manager does not recognise this site, and there is a reason. Read the address before going on.

actions.label: Close tab
actions.feedback: Right. The domain was idare-giris.example.net, not the office portal.

actions.label: Report site
actions.feedback: Great. Your report protects colleagues from the same link.

actions.label: Cancel
actions.feedback: Right, the manager caught the difference for you. Close the page and report it.

actions.label: Fill anyway
actions.feedback: Skipping the warning handed your password to a fake site. Change it now and report it.

steps.say: A link in an email takes you to a vault sign-in.

actions.label: Open vault
actions.feedback: Type the master password only in the ParolSeyf app itself. This site wanted your whole vault.

actions.label: Close tab
actions.feedback: Right. Open the vault by starting the app yourself, never through a link.

actions.label: Report site
actions.feedback: Great. This site may have been sent to several people.

scenes.prompt: Tap the signs that this email is fake.

subject.text: Your vault will be deleted in 24 hours

spots.label: Sender
spots.explain: The address is a look-alike, not ParolSeyf's domain.

spots.label: Deadline
spots.explain: A 24-hour threat is there to stop you thinking.

spots.label: Master password request
spots.explain: No service asks you to confirm your master password by email.

spots.label: Link
spots.explain: The link goes to a fake domain. Open the vault from the app yourself.

question.prompt: At night ParolSeyf asks you to approve a sign-in, but you are not signing in. What do you do?

options.label: I deny it and report it to security
options.feedback: Right. Someone knows your master password: change it now and let security check the sessions.

options.label: I approve so the requests stop
options.feedback: This is push bombing. One approval lets the attacker into the vault.

options.label: I ignore it and look in the morning
options.feedback: The request stays open, and someone already has your master password. Deny and report it now.

scenes.explain: An unexpected approval request means your password has leaked. Deny, report, change.

scenes.prompt: Match each situation with the right step.

pairs.right: Check the address, do not copy the password

pairs.left: An email link asks you to open the vault
You are on someone else's computer
pairs.right: Do not open your vault there

pairs.left: An approval request you did not expect

scenes.explain: The manager checks the address; you stop the moment it goes quiet.

points: If the manager offers no password, stop and check the address.
Type the master password only in the manager's own app, never via a link.
Deny approval requests you did not expect, and report them.
